definition_zh: 千克；公斤；一公斤的重量
definition_en: a unit of mass equal to one thousand grams, used for weighing goods and for the base unit of mass in the metric system
core_image: 菜市场台秤上的指针稳稳指向一公斤刻度的刻度盘
scene: 清晨的菜场刚开市，摊主把一袋土豆放上台秤。The needle stopped at one kilogram, so she wrote the price on the brown paper bag.
sceneCN: 这里 kilogram 是「千克、公斤」（第 1 个义项：质量单位，等于一千克），句意是指针停在一公斤处，于是她把价钱写在牛皮纸袋上。画面里有清晨的菜场、台秤和一袋土豆。

pos.zh: 名词：千克、公斤；一公斤的重量

derivatives.zh: 英式旧拼法，义为「千克、公斤」，与 kilogram 同义
kilogram 的日常缩略形式，义为「公斤」
kilogram 与 meter 合成的物理学单位，义为「千克米」

senses.title: The metric unit of mass
senses.definition: a unit of mass equal to one thousand grams
senses.definitionCN: 一千克的质量单位
senses.example: The parcel weighed just over three kilograms.
senses.exampleCN: 这个包裹重三公斤多一点。
senses.why: The metric system built its units in decimal steps from the gram, and a thousand grams named the practical everyday unit.
senses.whyCN: 公制以克为基准按十进制逐级扩展，一千克正好成为日常生活中最实用的那一级单位。

senses.title: A weight of that amount
senses.definition: an amount of something that weighs one thousand grams
senses.definitionCN: 重量等于一千克的某物的一份量
senses.example: She bought a kilogram of rice and a bunch of spring onions.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一公斤大米和一把小葱。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, people stop thinking of number and start using it as a measure of goods, like a bag of rice.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，人们就不再想数字，而直接把它当成货物的一份量，比如一袋米。

senses.title: The base unit in the metric system
senses.definition: since the redefinition of 2019, the kilogram is defined by a fundamental constant rather than by a metal block
senses.definitionCN: 自 2019 年重新定义起，千克改由基本物理常数定义，而不再以金属块为基准
senses.example: The kilogram is now tied to the Planck constant instead of a platinum cylinder.
senses.exampleCN: 千克现在与普朗克常数挂钩，而不再依赖铂铱圆柱体。
senses.why: For over a century a single metal cylinder served as the standard, and the word still names the base unit itself.
senses.whyCN: 一个多世纪里，一块金属圆柱就是标准，而这个词至今仍指这个基本单位本身。

intro.en: Kilogram is a French-built compound of a Greek prefix and a Latin root, created with the metric system at the end of the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: kilogram 是法语创造的合成词，由希腊语前缀与拉丁语词根构成，与十八世纪末的公制同时诞生。

items.en: Khilioi was the Greek word for a thousand, used in counting and in arithmetic.
items.cn: 希腊语 khilioi 表示「一千」，用于计数与算术。

items.en: Gramme entered French from Latin gramma, which meant a small weight, and was chosen for the base unit of mass.
items.cn: gramme 经拉丁语 gramma 进入法语，原指小重量，被选作质量的基本单位。

items.en: The metric commission joined kilo and gramme into kilogramme, the unit of a thousand grams.
items.cn: 公制委员会把 kilo 与 gramme 合成 kilogramme，即一千克的单位。

items.en: English took the French spelling, and the shorter kilogram became the everyday form, with kilo as its familiar clipping.
items.cn: 英语沿用了法语拼法，较短的 kilogram 成为日常写法，口语再缩略为 kilo。

items.en: In 2019 the standard block was retired and the kilogram was redefined by the Planck constant.
items.cn: 2019 年实物原器退役，千克改由普朗克常数重新定义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers metric words built on the same kilo element; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of stating weight.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带 kilo 这一构件的公制词；近义组收其他表示重量的说法。

entries.definition: A unit of distance; it shares the same thousand prefix but measures length.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位「千米」，共用「一千」这个前缀，但量的是长度。

entries.definition: The French-style spelling still used in British English for the same unit.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语仍在使用、源自法语的旧拼法，指同一个单位。

entries.definition: A unit of power, one thousand watts, built the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 功率单位「千瓦」，构词方式相同。

entries.definition: The base unit of mass, one thousandth of a kilogram.
entries.definitionCN: 质量的基础单位「克」，等于千分之一千克。

entries.definition: A unit of weight used in Britain and America, about four hundred and fifty grams.
entries.definitionCN: 英美使用的重量单位「磅」，约合四百五十克。

entries.definition: A metric unit of mass equal to one thousand kilograms.
entries.definitionCN: 公制质量单位「吨」，等于一千千克。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the real Greek thousand and the Latin gram to the everyday scenes where the unit appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把真实的希腊语「一千」与拉丁语 gram 连到这个词实际出现的日常场景。

normal.en: kilo is the Greek word for a thousand, so kilogram is literally a thousand grams.
normal.cn: kilo 是希腊语的「一千」，所以 kilogram 字面上就是一千克。

normal.en: The metric system climbs in tens: gram, then kilogram, then tonne.
normal.cn: 公制按十进位攀升：克、千克，再到吨。

normal.en: Shops shorten it to kilo: a kilo of apples is a kilogram of apples.
normal.cn: 商店里缩略成 kilo：一 kilo 苹果就是一公斤苹果。

normal.en: The symbol kg is written after the number, as in five kg.
normal.cn: 符号 kg 写在数字后面，如 five kg。

normal.en: Metre climbs by the same steps: kilometre is the thousand-metre cousin.
normal.cn: metre 按同样的台阶攀升：kilometre 就是「千米」这位表亲。

abstract.en: Picture a brass weight on a grocer scale with one mark after zero: the prefix says how many grams to stack there.
abstract.cn: 想象杂货秤上一枚铜砝码，刻度只到零后一格：前缀告诉你该在那里垒多少克。

abstract.en: The word is a pair of ideas, a thousand and a gram, pressed into a single block of sound.
abstract.cn: 这个词是两个概念——「一千」和「克」——压进同一块声音里。

abstract.en: Even the standard that the word points to has changed, yet the name stayed: the unit belongs to language now, not to the metal.
abstract.cn: 连这个词指向的标准都换过了，名字却留着：这个单位现在属于语言，而不属于那块金属。

examples.en: The baby weighed three kilograms at birth.
examples.cn: 这个婴儿出生时重三公斤。

examples.en: Please weigh out two kilograms of tomatoes.
examples.cn: 请称两公斤西红柿。

examples.en: One kilogram is about two point two pounds.
examples.cn: 一公斤约等于二点二磅。

dict_mnemonic.text: kilo 一千 + gram 克——一千克就是公斤

root: 法语 kilogramme，由希腊语 khilioi「一千」（作前缀 kilo-）与拉丁语 gramma「小的重量」（法语 gramme）合成；1795 年公制创制时期定名，2019 年起改用普朗克常数定义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the unit of mass, a weighed amount of that size, and the base unit itself as fixed by science.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：质量单位本身，一公斤重的一份货物，以及科学定义所依据的那个基本单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass weight on a scale settling exactly at the one kilogram mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上的铜砝码恰好落在「一公斤」的那道刻线上。

branches.en: THE UNIT: one thousand grams make one kilogram.
branches.cn: 单位线：一千克构成一公斤。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a bag of rice or tomatoes is weighed in kilograms.
branches.cn: 市场线：一袋米或西红柿按公斤称量。

branches.en: THE LAB: the base unit is now defined by a fixed constant.
branches.cn: 实验室线：基本单位如今由固定常数定义。

branches.en: THE NUMBER LINE: the word always pairs with a number or an amount.
branches.cn: 数字线：这个词总与数字或分量搭配。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL LINE: the short form kg travels on labels and packages.
branches.cn: 符号线：缩写在标签和包装上通行。

intro.en: Kilogram is a modern compound: a Greek number prefix, a Latin weight root used as a unit, and a few ordinary English shortenings.
intro.cn: kilogram 是近代合成词：希腊语数词前缀、被用作单位的拉丁语重量词根，以及几个普通的英语缩略形式。

latinIntro.en: The prefix kilo- is Greek, while gram comes from Latin gramma; both parts are recorded, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 kilo- 来自希腊语，gram 来自拉丁语 gramma；两部分均有文献记录，没有构拟成分。

items.example: It also builds kilometre and kilowatt.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 kilometre 与 kilowatt。

items.meaning: a small weight in metric use
items.meaningCN: 公制中的小重量单位「克」
items.example: Five hundred grams make half a kilogram.
The form kilogramme still appears in older texts.
items.exampleCN: kilogramme 这一形式仍见于较早的文本。

items.example: A kilo of apples is enough.

items.meaningCN: 表示「写、画之物」的构词成分
items.example: It appears in telegram and diagram.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 telegram 与 diagram。

items.example: Write five kg on the label.

latinEntries.meaning: a small weight, a written character

definition_en: to touch someone or something with the lips, or to touch something lightly, as a ball brushing the rim
core_image: 一个人俯身，用嘴唇轻轻贴上另一个人的脸颊
scene: 车站的月台上，母亲蹲下来与远行的女儿道别。She gave her daughter a quick kiss on the cheek before the train doors closed.
sceneCN: 这里 kiss 是「吻、亲吻」（第 1 个义项：用嘴唇接触表示亲爱或问候），句意是车门关上之前她在女儿脸颊上匆匆一吻。画面里有车站月台、母亲与女儿。

pos.zh: 名词：吻；一下亲吻
动词：亲吻；轻触、轻碰

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「接吻、亲吻」
由动词加 -er 构成，口语中指「亲吻的人」，也指嘴
加 -able 构成，义为「值得一吻的、可爱亲人的」
合成说法，义为「披露私情的」

senses.title: To touch with the lips
senses.definition: to touch a person or thing with the lips as a sign of love, greeting, or respect
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰人或物以表示爱意、问候或敬意
senses.example: He kissed his mother on the forehead before leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 他离开前吻了母亲的额头。
senses.why: The core act is a small, soft touch of the lips, the most intimate gesture of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是嘴唇一次轻而柔的触碰，是嘴部最亲密的动作。

senses.title: The act or sound of kissing
senses.definition: an act of touching someone with the lips, or the sound of such a touch
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴唇触碰某人的行为，或这种触碰发出的声音
senses.example: She sent the children a kiss before bedtime.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们睡前她送了他们一个吻。
senses.why: The verb became a noun by naming the gesture itself, a pattern English uses again and again.
senses.whyCN: 动词直接名词化，用这个手势本身来命名，这是英语反复使用的模式。

senses.title: To touch lightly
senses.definition: to touch something very lightly, the way lips would, without pressing
senses.definitionCN: 像嘴唇那样极轻地接触某物，而不用力
senses.example: The ball kissed the top of the crossbar and went over.
senses.exampleCN: 球轻擦横梁上沿然后飞了出去。
senses.why: Because a kiss is barely a touch, the word extends to anything that grazes another surface.
senses.whyCN: 因为吻几乎算不上用力一碰，这个词便延伸到任何擦过另一表面的东西。

senses.title: To part from someone with a kiss
senses.definition: in the phrase kiss goodbye, to depart from someone with a kiss, or to give something up
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 kiss goodbye，指吻别，也指放弃某物
senses.example: You can kiss goodbye to your quiet weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以跟你安静的周末告别了。
senses.why: The farewell kiss became a compact idiom, and the second meaning treats a lost thing as something kissed away.
senses.whyCN: 告别的吻凝固成习语，第二个意思则把失去的东西当作被吻走的东西。

intro.en: Kiss is an old Germanic word, recorded in English before the Norman conquest and related to the verbs still used in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: kiss 是古老的日耳曼语词，在诺曼征服前已有英语记录，与德语、荷兰语里仍在使用的动词同源。

items.en: The verb appears as cyssan, with the noun coss, in the earliest English texts.
items.cn: 这个动词在最早的英语文本里写作 cyssan，名词为 coss。

items.en: The same root is found in German küssen and Dutch kussen, which shows a common Germanic origin.
items.cn: 同一词根见于德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen，说明它源自共同的日耳曼语。

items.en: Northern and eastern dialects kept short forms of the word, which fed the Middle English spelling with k.
items.cn: 北部与东部方言保留了短暂的词形，为中古英语带 k 的拼法提供了来源。

items.en: The form settle between Old and Modern English as kissen and kisse.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，词形定作 kissen 与 kisse，处在古英语与现代英语之间。

items.en: English keeps the word for the gesture and adds idioms such as kiss goodbye and kiss and make up.
items.cn: 英语保留了这个手势词，并增添了 kiss goodbye、kiss and make up 等习语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that differ from kiss by one or two letters; the near-meaning group collects other words for affection shown with the body or the lips.
note.cn: 形近组收与 kiss 相差一两个字母的词；近义组收以身体或嘴唇表达亲昵的其他词。

entries.definition: Formed directly from kiss with the suffix -able, meaning worth kissing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 kiss 加 -able 直接构成，义为「值得一吻的」。

entries.definition: An old Scottish word for a chest, spelled like the past tense of kiss.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰语里指「箱子」的旧词，拼法与 kiss 的过去式相同。

entries.definition: A fruit jelly once served at Russian meals, unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 曾经出现在俄式餐桌上的果冻，词源与 kiss 无关。

entries.definition: To hold someone in the arms, a bigger and more whole-bodied gesture.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人抱在怀里，动作更大、更整体。

entries.definition: A quick, light kiss, named after the bird.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快的一下亲吻，由鸟啄食的动作得名。

entries.definition: To touch someone gently with the hand, without the lips.
entries.definitionCN: 用手轻柔地抚摸，不涉及嘴唇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic family and the set phrases in which the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的日耳曼语词族，以及这个词实际出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Kiss doubles the s before -es and -ed: kisses, kissed.
normal.cn: kiss 在加 -es 和 -ed 前要双写 s：kisses、kissed。

normal.en: German küssen and Dutch kussen keep the same root alive.
normal.cn: 德语 küssen 与荷兰语 kussen 把同一词根延续下来。

normal.en: The noun takes a modifier: a quick kiss, a goodbye kiss, a kiss on the cheek.
normal.cn: 名词常带修饰语：a quick kiss、a goodbye kiss、a kiss on the cheek。

normal.en: Blow a kiss sends the gesture through the air instead of the lips.
normal.cn: blow a kiss 是把这一手势吹出去，而不是用嘴唇贴上。

normal.en: A ball that grazes the rim is said to kiss it.
normal.cn: 擦过篮圈的球被说成对它 kiss 了一下。

abstract.en: A kiss is the smallest possible contact: two surfaces almost touching, and nothing more.
abstract.cn: 吻是可能的最轻的接触：两个表面几乎贴上，仅此而已。

abstract.en: The same word covers love and geometry; the gentleness is what the two have in common.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指爱情也指几何：两者的共同点就是那份轻。

abstract.en: To kiss something goodbye is to accept that it will not come back, as a farewell kiss marks a parting.
abstract.cn: kiss something goodbye 就是承认它不会回来，正如告别的一吻标志分离。

examples.en: She kissed her son goodnight.
examples.cn: 她吻了儿子，道一声晚安。

examples.en: The first kiss came after the film ended.
examples.cn: 电影散场后他们有了第一次亲吻。

examples.en: The shuttlecock kissed the net and dropped over.
examples.cn: 羽毛球轻擦球网后落到了对面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可斯」——轻轻可斯的一下，就是亲吻

root: 古英语 cyssan（动词）与 coss（名词），源自共同日耳曼语词根，同源于德语 küssen、荷兰语 kussen；中古英语写作 kissen、kisse，现代英语固定为 kiss，并引申出轻触与吻别义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the lips touching as a sign of love, the gesture as a noun, any very light contact, and the farewell idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：以唇触碰表示亲爱，作为名词的手势本身，任何极轻的接触，以及告别的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips resting for a moment on a cheek, the lightest touch the body makes.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇在脸颊上停留一瞬，是身体能做出的最轻的触碰。

branches.en: THE LIPS LINE: the mouth touches as a sign of love, greeting or respect.
branches.cn: 唇线：嘴部触碰，表示爱意、问候或敬意。

branches.en: THE GESTURE LINE: the touch becomes a countable thing people give and send.
branches.cn: 手势线：这份触碰变成可以送出、可以计数的一个东西。

branches.en: THE GRAZE LINE: anything that barely touches, from a ball to a breeze, borrows the word.
branches.cn: 擦碰线：从球到微风，任何几乎贴上的东西都借用这个词。

branches.en: THE PARTING LINE: the farewell kiss turns into an idiom for giving something up.
branches.cn: 离别线：告别的吻变成放弃某物的习语。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: the Germanic cousins keep the same root in German and Dutch.
branches.cn: 词族线：德语与荷兰语的同源词保留着同一词根。

intro.en: Kiss is a native Germanic word that grows mainly by inflection and by a few suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: kiss 是日耳曼本土词，主要靠词形变化以及少数后缀与合成来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Kiss has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are given only as contrasts for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: kiss 没有拉丁语祖先，下面这些拉丁词只是同一概念的对照。

items.example: The couple were kissing in the rain.
A kiss-and-tell article ruined his career.
items.exampleCN: 一篇披露私情的文章毁了他的事业。

items.example: They kissed goodbye at the gate.

definition_zh: 成套工具；工具箱；配套元件；装备
definition_en: a set of parts or tools kept together for a particular purpose, or the equipment a person carries for an activity
core_image: 一只敞开的帆布箱，工具、零件与说明按格摆齐
scene: 车停在山路边熄了火，后备箱里那只帆布包派上了用场。He opened the repair kit and found a spare belt and a small torch in it.
sceneCN: 这里 kit 是「成套工具、工具箱」（第 1 个义项：为某用途配套收纳的一套工具或零件），句意是他打开修理包，在里面找到一条备用皮带和一只小手电。画面里有山路、熄火的车和敞开的帆布包。

pos.zh: 名词：成套工具；配套元件；装备
动词：装备（用 kit out、kit up 搭配）

derivatives.zh: kit 的复数形式，义为「多套工具或装备」
由动词加 -ed 构成，英式口语义为「装备齐全的」
kit 与 bag 合成，义为「行囊、工具袋」
外形相近但词源不同，义为「厨房」

senses.title: A set of tools kept together
senses.definition: a set of tools, parts, or equipment packed together for a specific job
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途配套收纳的工具、零件或装备
senses.example: Every car should carry a basic tool kit.
senses.exampleCN: 每辆车都该带一套基本工具。
senses.why: The word started as a wooden tub for holding a soldier things, and the container came to stand for the set it held.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指装士兵杂物的木盆，容器后来代表它所装的那一整套。

senses.title: Equipment for an activity
senses.definition: the clothes and equipment that a person needs for a sport, a job, or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 个人从事运动、工作或旅行所需的衣物与器具
senses.example: His football kit was drying on the radiator.
senses.exampleCN: 他的足球装备正在暖气片上晾着。
senses.why: Once it named a soldier belongings, the word naturally widened to anyone gear for a task.
senses.whyCN: 它既曾指士兵的随身之物，扩而广之指任何人做某件事的行头。

senses.title: Parts sold ready to assemble
senses.definition: a set of parts sold together to be put together by the buyer, as for a model or furniture
senses.definitionCN: 一起出售、由购买者自行组装的零件，如模型或家具
senses.example: The shelf came as a kit with screws and a diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 这个架子以套件形式出售，附螺丝和图解。
senses.why: In trade the container word turned into a commercial unit: everything you need, sold in one box.
senses.whyCN: 在买卖里，容器词变成了一个出售单位：所需之物全装在一只箱子里卖出。

senses.title: To equip someone
senses.definition: in the phrases kit out and kit up, to provide someone with clothes or equipment
senses.definitionCN: 用于 kit out、kit up，指为某人提供衣物或装备
senses.example: The team was kitted out in new shirts.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍换上了整套新球衣。
senses.why: From the noun of supplies came the verb of handing them out, a frequent path in English.
senses.whyCN: 由补给品之名的名词生出「发放补给」的动词，这是英语里常见的一条路。

intro.en: Kit appears in late Middle English as the name of a wooden tub, and the history before that is debated.
intro.cn: kit 在中古英语晚期以「木盆」之义出现，再往前的来历尚有争议。

items.en: Kyt or kit named a wooden tub or tankard used for holding liquids or provisions.
items.cn: kyt 或 kit 指盛液体或食物的木盆、木桶。

items.en: The closest early relative is the Middle Dutch kitte, a wooden tub made of staves, which supports a Dutch source.
items.cn: 最早的近亲是中古荷兰语 kitte，一种板条拼成的木盆，这支持荷兰语来源说。

items.en: A link with German Kütze or with Old French cuve has also been proposed, and scholars do not fully agree.
items.cn: 也有人提出与德语 Kütze 或古法语 cuve 有关，学界尚未取得一致。

items.en: Soldiers carried a kit, and from the tub the name shifted to the whole set of personal gear.
items.cn: 士兵随身带着 kit，名字由木盆转到了整套个人装备上。

items.en: In the twentieth century kit became the standard word for a boxed set of parts, from models to medical supplies.
items.cn: 二十世纪里 kit 成为「盒装成套零件」的标准说法，从模型到医疗用品都用它。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ from kit by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a prepared set.
note.cn: 形近组收与 kit 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「备好的一套」的说法。

entries.definition: One letter apart; it names the flying toy and a bird of prey.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指风筝以及一种猛禽。

entries.definition: Adds a syllable to kit and names a young cat.
entries.definitionCN: 在 kit 后多加一个音节，指小猫。

entries.definition: Differs by one letter and means a young goat or, informally, a child.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，指小山羊，口语中也指孩子。

entries.definition: A group of things used together, wider and more neutral than kit.
entries.definitionCN: 一起使用的一组物品，范围更宽、语体更中性。

entries.definition: A container of goods sold or carried together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起出售或携带的一包物品。

entries.definition: Equipment for an activity, usually uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 某项活动所用的装备，通常不可数。

normalIntro.en: The hooks connect the wooden tub, the soldier bag and the modern boxed set that the word has named in turn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把木盆、士兵行囊与现代盒装套件依次连起来，这几个东西都曾被这个词指称。

normal.en: Kit doubles the t before -ed and -ing: kitted, kitting.
normal.cn: kit 在加 -ed、-ing 前要双写 t：kitted、kitting。

normal.en: The word once meant a wooden tub; the container still leads to the contents.
normal.cn: 这个词曾指木盆；容器仍然指向它所装的东西。

normal.en: First-aid kit and tool kit are the two phrases you will meet most.
normal.cn: first-aid kit 与 tool kit 是最常遇到的两个搭配。

normal.en: Kit out is the verb form: to fit someone out with gear.
normal.cn: kit out 是动词用法：给某人配齐装备。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with kitchen, which is only a look-alike, not a relative.
normal.cn: 别与厨房 kitchen 混淆，后者只是形近，并非同源。

abstract.en: A kit is a promise of readiness: everything has its place before the need arrives.
abstract.cn: 一套 kit 就是一份「已准备好」的承诺：在需要到来之前，一切各就各位。

abstract.en: The word moves from the box to what is in it, the way a toolbox can stand for the tools.
abstract.cn: 这个词从箱子走到箱中之物，正如工具箱可以代表工具本身。

abstract.en: Parts in a kit are potential: they become a shelf or a model only when someone puts them together.
abstract.cn: 套件里的零件只是潜能：有人把它们拼起来，才成为架子或模型。

examples.en: Take a first-aid kit on the hike.
examples.cn: 徒步时带上一只急救箱。

examples.en: The model plane came as a kit for beginners.
examples.cn: 这架模型飞机以适合初学者的套件形式出售。

examples.en: The club kitted out the new players in matching shirts.
examples.cn: 俱乐部给新队员配齐了统一球衣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「齐特」——齐全的特殊物件，装成一箱就是成套工具

root: 中古英语 kyt / kit 指木盆、木桶，可能来自中古荷兰语 kitte（板条木盆），也有德语或古法语来源的猜测，尚无定论；后指士兵的随身行囊，再引申为「一整套工具、装备、套件」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the set of tools in a container, a person own equipment, a boxed set of parts to assemble, and the verb of equipping.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：装在容器里的一套工具，个人装备，盒装配件，以及「给某人配装备」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open canvas box with every tool and part in its own slot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只敞开的帆布箱，工具与零件各在各自的格子里。

branches.en: THE TOOLS: the set is kept together so that a job can be done at once.
branches.cn: 工具线：整套放在一起，随时可以动手。

branches.en: THE PERSON: gear for a sport or journey belongs to one body.
branches.cn: 个人线：运动或旅行的装备归属于一个人。

branches.en: THE BOX SALE: parts sold together, to be built at home.
branches.cn: 盒装线：零件一起出售，由买者在家里装好。

branches.en: THE VERB LINE: the noun of supplies gives a verb of handing them out.
branches.cn: 动词线：补给品之名生出「发放补给」的动词。

branches.en: THE OLD TUB: the container image still explains why a kit holds a set.
branches.cn: 旧木盆线：容器的意象仍能解释为什么 kit 装着一整套。

intro.en: Kit is a short native noun that grows by inflection and by compounds rather than by Latin affixes.
intro.cn: kit 是短小的本土名词，靠词形变化与合成扩展，而非拉丁语词缀。

latinIntro.en: Kit has no Latin source; the tub words below are given only as historical neighbours.
latinIntro.cn: kit 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些「桶、盆」词只作为历史上的近邻列出。

items.meaning: a set of tools or gear

items.example: Both kits are on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 两个工具箱都在架子上。

items.example: The team is kitted and ready.
items.exampleCN: 队伍装备齐整，准备就绪。

items.example: Kitting out a new lab takes weeks.
items.exampleCN: 给新实验室配齐装备要花好几周。

items.meaningCN: 与 kit 构成 kit out
items.exampleCN: 它补足 kit out 这一搭配。

items.meaningCN: 与 kit 构成 kit up
items.exampleCN: 它补足 kit up 这一搭配。

items.example: He threw his kitbag on the bus.
items.exampleCN: 他把行李袋扔上了巴士。
它把 kit 变成 kits。

latinEntries.structure: Medieval Latin noun from Latin cupa

definition_zh: 厨房；烹饪部门；某种风味的菜系
definition_en: the room where food is prepared and cooked, and by extension the cooking staff or the cuisine of a place
core_image: 灶台上蒸汽升腾，案板、锅铲与菜刀各在其位
scene: 傍晚的出租屋里，油烟机低声作响，水汽模糊了窗。In the tiny kitchen a pot of soup was simmering while she chopped spring onions on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 kitchen 是「厨房」（第 1 个义项：做饭做菜的房间），句意是在这间小厨房里一锅汤正炖着，她在案板上切小葱。画面里有傍晚的出租屋、油烟机和水汽。

pos.zh: 名词：厨房；炊事人员；菜系

derivatives.zh: kitchen 加指小后缀构成，义为「小厨房」
kitchen 与 ware 合成，义为「厨房用具」
古词，义为「管厨房的人」

senses.title: The room where food is cooked
senses.definition: the room in a house or restaurant used for preparing and cooking food
senses.definitionCN: 住宅或餐馆里用于备餐与烹饪的房间
senses.example: The smell of garlic filled the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 蒜香充满了厨房。
senses.why: The word names the place itself, the room built around fire and water for cooking.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指地方本身：围绕火与水而建、专门用于做饭的那个房间。

senses.title: The cooking staff of a place
senses.definition: the people who work in a kitchen, especially the cooks of a restaurant or hotel
senses.definitionCN: 在厨房工作的人，尤指餐馆或酒店的厨师团队
senses.example: The kitchen was praised for serving hot food all night.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房因整夜供应热食而受到称赞。
senses.why: In a restaurant the room and the people inside it are spoken of as one unit, so a good team simply becomes a good kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 在餐馆里，房间和里面的人被当作一个整体来说，于是好团队干脆就被称作好厨房。

senses.title: A regional style of cooking
senses.definition: the food and cooking style of a country or region
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区的菜肴与烹饪风格
senses.example: She loves the Sichuan kitchen for its heat.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢川菜那股辣劲。
senses.why: Chefs began to speak of a whole national cuisine as a kitchen, and the metaphor stayed in food writing.
senses.whyCN: 厨师们开始把一个国家的整套烹饪称为一个 kitchen，这个比喻留在了饮食写作里。

intro.en: Kitchen descends from Latin coquina through Old English, and every step of the chain is recorded.
intro.cn: kitchen 由拉丁语 coquina 经古英语一路传来，这条链条的每一环都有文献记录。

items.en: Coquina was the Latin word for a kitchen, and coquere meant to cook or prepare food with heat.
items.cn: coquina 是拉丁语「厨房」，动词 coquere 意为用火烹煮。

items.en: English borrowed the food word early as cycene, with the same cooking sense as the Latin.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个词，写作 cycene，烹饪义与拉丁语相同。

items.en: Norse speakers in the ninth and tenth centuries reshaped the word, and their form lies behind the modern spelling.
items.cn: 九、十世纪的北欧移民改造了这个词形，现代拼法源自他们的形式。

items.en: Kitchene appears as the home room and, in great houses, as the whole cooking department.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 kitchene，既指家中的房间，也指大宅里整个厨房班子。

items.en: The word widens into cookbooks and menus: kitchen now also names a cuisine, as in the Italian kitchen.
items.cn: 这个词延伸到菜谱与菜单里：如今 kitchen 也指一种菜系，如意大利菜系。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin or end like kitchen; the near-meaning group gathers other rooms and places for food.
note.cn: 形近组收开头或结尾像 kitchen 的词；近义组收其他与食物有关的房间与场所。

entries.definition: The word plus a small-size suffix, meaning a tiny kitchen.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加表示「小」的后缀，义为「小厨房」。

entries.definition: Shares the first letters, but names a young cat.
entries.definitionCN: 前半段相同，指的是小猫。

entries.definition: An old word for a person in charge of a kitchen.
entries.definitionCN: 旧词，指负责管厨房的人。

entries.definition: A small room for storing food and dishes, not for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 储存食物与餐具的小房间，不做饭。

entries.definition: The kitchen of a ship or an aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 船或飞机上的厨房。

entries.definition: A place where meals are served to a group, such as workers or students.
entries.definitionCN: 为工人、学生等群体供餐的食堂。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin and Old English chain and the phrases the word appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用有据可查的拉丁语与古英语链条，以及这个词现在的常见搭配。

normal.en: Latin coquere meant to cook, and its noun coquina was the kitchen.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 coquere 意为「煮」，其名词 coquina 就是厨房。

normal.en: Old English wrote it cycene, then Norse speakers changed the sound.
normal.cn: 古英语写作 cycene，后来北欧移民改变了读音。

normal.en: A kitchenette is a kitchen cut down to a corner.
normal.cn: kitchenette 就是缩到一角的小厨房。

normal.en: Kitchenware is everything in the kitchen except the food.
normal.cn: kitchenware 是厨房里除了食物以外的一切。

normal.en: In restaurants the word means the staff, not just the room.
normal.cn: 在餐馆里这个词指那班人，而不只是房间。

abstract.en: A kitchen is a room built as a tool: cupboards, heat, water and a surface to work on.
abstract.cn: 厨房像一件被盖成房间的工具：柜子、火、水，以及一块干活的面。

abstract.en: Of all the rooms in a house, only this one is named after the verb for cooking.
abstract.cn: 一栋房子的所有房间里，只有它是以「烹饪」这个动词的祖先命名的。

abstract.en: Order in the kitchen is a small image of order in the household: food ready when people need it.
abstract.cn: 厨房里的秩序是家庭秩序的小小缩影：人在需要时，饭已备好。

examples.en: The children ate breakfast in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房吃了早饭。

examples.en: The hotel kitchen serves dinner until eleven.
examples.cn: 酒店厨房供餐到十一点。

examples.en: This book explores the Italian kitchen region by region.
examples.cn: 这本书按地区逐一考察意大利菜系。

dict_mnemonic.text: kitchen 里总有 chicken——厨房里总有鸡肉香

root: 古英语 cycene，源自拉丁语 coquina（厨房）、coquere（烹煮），并受古北欧语形式改造；中古英语 kitchene，现代英语 kitchen，后引申指厨房人员与菜系。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the room, the team who work there, and a whole cuisine seen as one kitchen.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：那个房间，在那里工作的一班人，以及被看作一个厨房的一整套菜系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steam over a pot, knives and boards laid out, the room built for cooking.
core.cn: 核心意象：锅上蒸汽升腾，刀与案板各就各位，这是为做饭而建的房间。

branches.en: THE ROOM: the place with heat, water and work surfaces.
branches.cn: 房间线：有火、有水、有操作台的地方。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: in trade the word stands for the cooks as a body.
branches.cn: 人员线：在行业内这个词代表作为整体的厨师。

branches.en: THE CUISINE: a whole food culture can be spoken of as one kitchen.
branches.cn: 菜系线：整套饮食文化可以说成一个厨房。

branches.en: THE LATIN LINE: cook and kitchen come from the same root, coquere.
branches.cn: 拉丁线：cook 与 kitchen 同出一根，即 coquere。

branches.en: THE SMALL FORM: a kitchenette is the same room in miniature.
branches.cn: 小型线：kitchenette 是同一个房间的缩小版。

intro.en: Kitchen is an inherited Latin-French-Norse word, and English extends it with diminutive and compound forms.
intro.cn: kitchen 是经拉丁语、古法语与北欧语传下的固有词，英语用指小与合成形式扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Latin coquere and coquina are recorded, as are the derived forms below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 coquere 与 coquina 均有记录，下面这些派生形式也同样有据。

items.example: It is part of the Latin source.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语源词的一部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to cook, to prepare food with heat

definition_zh: 膝；膝盖；膝部；裤子的膝部
definition_en: the joint between the thigh and the lower leg, the front part of that joint, or the part of a garment covering it
core_image: 一条腿在弯折处凸起的硬骨，屈伸之间承担全身重量
scene: 球场上有人被铲倒，抱着腿蜷在草皮上。He fell on his knee and stayed down for a moment before standing up again.
sceneCN: 这里 knee 是「膝盖、膝关节」（第 1 个义项：大腿与小腿之间的关节），句意是他跪倒在地，停了一会儿才重新站起来。画面里有球场草皮与受伤的球员。

pos.zh: 名词：膝；膝关节；膝部；裤膝

derivatives.zh: 与 knee 同源的动词，义为「跪下」
knee 与 deep 合成，义为「深及膝盖的」
knee 与 cap 合成，义为「膝盖骨」
合成词，义为「条件反射式的、不经思考的」

senses.title: The joint of the leg
senses.definition: the joint where the thigh and the lower leg meet, which allows the leg to bend
senses.definitionCN: 大腿与小腿相接、能让腿弯曲的关节
senses.example: The old injury still makes his knee ache in cold weather.
senses.exampleCN: 旧伤让他的膝盖一到冷天就疼。
senses.why: The joint is the body part the word first named, and all other senses grow from it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早命名的就是这处关节，其他义项都由它生长出来。

senses.title: The front of the knee
senses.definition: the front area of the leg around that joint, where a person kneels
senses.definitionCN: 关节周围的腿部前侧，人下跪时着地的部位
senses.example: She rested the baby on her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 她把婴儿放在膝上。
senses.why: Because the front of the joint is what people rest things on, the same word names the lap-like surface.
senses.whyCN: 由于关节前侧是人放东西的地方，同一个词也用来指这块近似膝盖上的台面。

senses.title: The part of a garment over the knee
senses.definition: the part of a trouser leg that covers the knee
senses.definitionCN: 裤腿上覆盖膝盖的那一段
senses.example: The boy always wore out the knees of his trousers.
senses.exampleCN: 那男孩总把裤子的膝部磨破。
senses.why: Clothing takes the names of the body parts it covers, so trousers have knees as people do.
senses.whyCN: 衣物会借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名，所以裤子也有膝盖。

intro.en: Knee is an old Germanic body word whose k has been silent for centuries; related words survive in German and Dutch.
intro.cn: knee 是古老的日耳曼语身体词，词首的 k 已沉默数百年；相关词在德语与荷兰语中留存。

items.en: The noun was cneo, and the related verb cneowian meant to kneel.
items.cn: 名词写作 cneo，相关的动词 cneowian 意为「跪下」。

items.en: German Knie and Dutch knie show the same word in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 德语 Knie 与荷兰语 knie 显示同一词在日耳曼语其他分支中的样貌。

items.en: The spelling became kne and knes, and the k stopped being pronounced before the vowel.
items.cn: 拼法变为 kne 与 knes，词首的 k 在元音前已不再发音。

items.en: The silent k and the long vowel make knee look unlike the way it sounds.
items.cn: 不发音的 k 与长元音让 knee 的写法与读音显得很不一样。

items.en: English builds compounds from it, among them kneecap and knee-deep.
items.cn: 英语用它构成合成词，如 kneecap 与 knee-deep。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent k or a similar ending; the near-meaning group gathers other joints and related body words.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带不发音 k 或结尾相近的词；近义组收其他关节与相关身体词。

entries.definition: The verb from the same Old English root, meaning to go down on the knees.
entries.definitionCN: 与 knee 同出古英语词根的动词，义为「跪」。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k, but means to work dough with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，意为用手揉面团。

entries.definition: Another silent-k word, naming a cutting tool.
entries.definitionCN: 又一个 k 不发音的词，指刀具。

entries.definition: The part of the leg above the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以上的那段腿，即大腿。

entries.definition: The front of the lower leg below the knee.
entries.definitionCN: 膝以下小腿的前面。

entries.definition: The joint of the arm, the knee of the upper limb.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂的关节，上肢的「膝」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English form, the silent k, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的古英语词形、不发音的 k，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Old English cneo already had the k, which later went silent.
normal.cn: 古英语 cneo 本就带 k，后来这个音沉默了。

normal.en: German Knie keeps the k spoken, while English dropped the sound.
normal.cn: 德语 Knie 仍把 k 读出来，英语则把它丢掉。

normal.en: On one knee is the pose of a proposal or of rest.
normal.cn: on one knee 是求婚或歇息时的姿势。

normal.en: Kneecap and knee-deep are built straight from the body part.
normal.cn: kneecap 与 knee-deep 直接由这个身体部位构成。

normal.en: Trousers wear out at the knees, exactly where the body bends.
normal.cn: 裤子总在膝部磨破，那里正是身体弯折之处。

abstract.en: A knee is a hinge: the whole body weight travels through a joint the size of a fist.
abstract.cn: 膝盖是一处铰链：全身重量都经过这样一个拳头大小的关节。

abstract.en: The word is the same for the joint, the lap and the cloth over it, because clothing follows the body.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指关节、膝上，也指膝上的布，因为衣物是跟着身体走的。

abstract.en: Bending the knee is the oldest gesture of respect, which is why the verb kneel carries such weight.
abstract.cn: 屈膝是最古老的敬意姿态，所以动词 kneel 才有那样的分量。

examples.en: He hurt his knee during the match.
examples.cn: 他在比赛中伤到了膝盖。

examples.en: The child sat on her father knee and listened.
examples.cn: 孩子坐在父亲膝上听着。

examples.en: These trousers have reinforced knees.
examples.cn: 这条裤子的膝部做了加固。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泥」——跪在泥里，最先沾泥的就是膝盖

root: 古英语 cneo（膝），源自共同日耳曼语，同源于德语 Knie、荷兰语 knie；中古英语作 kne，词首 k 在元音前逐渐不发音，现代英语扩展出 kneecap、knee-deep 等合成词。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the joint itself, the lap-like front of it, and the part of a garment that covers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：关节本身，关节前侧那块像膝上的台面，以及覆盖它的那段衣料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard knob at the bend of the leg, carrying the body as it folds.
core.cn: 核心意象：腿弯处一块坚硬的凸起，在身体折叠时承担重量。

branches.en: THE JOINT: the hinge where thigh and shin meet.
branches.cn: 关节线：大腿与小腿相接的铰链。

branches.en: THE LAP: the front of the joint is where children and books rest.
branches.cn: 膝上线：关节前侧是放孩子、放书的地方。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: garments take the name of the body part they cover.
branches.cn: 布料线：衣物借用它所覆盖的身体部位之名。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the silent k marks the Germanic history of the word.
branches.cn: 读音线：不发音的 k 标出了这个词的日耳曼来历。

branches.en: THE POSTURE LINE: kneeling and sitting on the knee both begin at this joint.
branches.cn: 姿态线：下跪与坐在膝上，都从这处关节开始。

intro.en: Knee is an inherited Germanic noun; its family is built by inflection and by compounds such as kneecap.
intro.cn: knee 是继承而来的日耳曼名词，其词族靠词形变化以及 kneecap 一类合成构成。

latinIntro.en: Knee has no Latin source, so the Latin joint words below are offered as contrasts only.
latinIntro.cn: knee 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语关节词仅作对照。

items.meaning: the bone in front of the joint
deep enough to reach the knees
to go down on the knees

items.exampleCN: 它把 knee 变成 knees。

definition_en: to go down or rest on one or both knees, as in prayer, respect, or obedience
core_image: 礼拜堂里一个人双膝落地，脊背挺直，头微微低下
scene: 老教堂的长椅之间，木地板被磨得发亮。She knelt beside the pew and prayed quietly for a long minute.
sceneCN: 这里 kneel 是「跪下、跪着」（第 1 个义项：用膝盖着地），句意是她在长椅旁跪下，安静地祷告了很长一分钟。画面里有老教堂、长椅与磨亮的木地板。

pos.zh: 动词：跪下；跪着；屈膝（表示敬意或服从）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「跪姿、跪着」
加 -er 构成，义为「跪垫、下跪的人」
与 kneel 同源的名词，义为「膝盖」

senses.title: To go down on the knees
senses.definition: to go down onto the knees or rest with the weight on them
senses.definitionCN: 用膝盖着地，或把身体重量压在膝上
senses.example: He knelt down to tie the child shoe.
senses.exampleCN: 他跪下给孩子系鞋带。
senses.why: The verb describes the movement of the body onto its knee, a posture reached from standing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词描述身体下沉到膝盖上的动作，是一种从站立到达的姿势。

senses.title: To show respect or submission
senses.definition: to kneel as a sign of reverence toward a person, a god, or a power
senses.definitionCN: 为向人、神或权力表示敬意而下跪
senses.example: The knights knelt before the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士们在女王面前跪下。
senses.why: Because lowering the body means lowering oneself, the plain posture became the gesture of respect and surrender.
senses.whyCN: 因为压低身体就意味着压低自己，这一姿势便成为敬意与臣服的姿态。

senses.title: To pray while kneeling
senses.definition: to pray with the body on the knees, as many traditions do
senses.definitionCN: 像许多传统那样，双膝落地地祈祷
senses.example: The whole family knelt together every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人每晚一起跪下祷告。
senses.why: Prayer made the posture a routine, so the verb often implies what is being done in that position.
senses.whyCN: 祷告让这种姿势成了常规，所以这个动词常暗含在这个姿势里所做的事。

intro.en: Kneel is the verb matching the noun knee, and both come from one Old English root.
intro.cn: kneel 是与名词 knee 相配的动词，二者出自同一个古英语词根。

items.en: The verb cneowlian described going down on the knees, beside the noun cneo.
items.cn: 动词 cneowlian 描述跪下的动作，与名词 cneo 并列。

items.en: Northern texts also show cneolian, and both forms share the silent k of the noun family.
items.cn: 北部文本又见 cneolian，两种形式都带着词族中不发音的 k。

items.en: The form settles as knelen, and the past tense knelede later shrinks to knelt.
items.cn: 词形定为 knelen，过去式 knelede 后来缩为 knelt。

items.en: English keeps knelt as the usual past tense, with kneeled as a common American variant.
items.cn: 英语以 knelt 为常用过去式，kneeled 则是常见的美式变体。

items.en: The verb is now used for prayer, respect, obedience, and the practical act of getting low to work.
items.cn: 如今这个动词用于祈祷、致敬、服从，以及低身干活这样的实用动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent k and the same vowel; the near-meaning group gathers postures and related actions.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带不发音的 k 与同样元音的词；近义组收其他姿势与相关动作。

entries.definition: The noun from the same Old English root, naming the joint that bends.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古英语词根的名词，指那处会弯的关节。

entries.definition: Sounds almost the same but means to press and fold dough.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，但意思是按压折叠面团。

entries.definition: Written without the n, and names the spine of a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 少了 n，指船的龙骨。

entries.definition: To bend low with the knees, keeping the feet flat.
entries.definitionCN: 屈膝低身，脚掌着地。

entries.definition: To sit with the knees bent and the weight on the feet, without the knees touching the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 屈膝坐着，重量落在脚上，膝盖不触地。

entries.definition: To bend the upper body as a greeting or sign of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 弯下上半身表示问候或敬意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English pair, the two past forms, and the scenes where kneeling happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的古英语一对词、两种过去式，以及下跪实际发生的场景。

normal.en: Kneel and knee come from the same Old English root; the verb is the noun in motion.
normal.cn: kneel 与 knee 同出古英语词根；动词就是运动中的名词。

normal.en: The k is silent, just as in knee, knife and knock.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knife、knock 一样。

normal.en: British English prefers knelt; American English also uses kneeled.
normal.cn: 英式英语偏好 knelt，美式英语也用 kneeled。

normal.en: Kneel down adds nothing in meaning but adds the direction of the movement.
normal.cn: kneel down 没有增加意义，只补出动作的方向。

normal.en: Kneeling in prayer is the most common use of the word.
normal.cn: 祈祷时下跪是这个词最常见的用法。

abstract.en: Going down on the knees is the shortest way to make oneself smaller than the person in front.
abstract.cn: 双膝落地是把自己在对方面前压低的最短路径。

abstract.en: The posture is a sentence without words: the body says what the mouth might not.
abstract.cn: 这个姿势是一句不用词的话：身体说出嘴未必说出的意思。

abstract.en: The same verb covers prayer and tying a shoelace, since the body does not know the difference.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既指祈祷也指系鞋带，因为身体不做这种区分。

examples.en: She knelt to look the child in the eye.
examples.cn: 她蹲跪下来，与孩子平视。

examples.en: The crowd knelt as the procession passed.
examples.cn: 队伍经过时人群跪下。

examples.en: He was still kneeling in the garden when the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨下起来时他还在花园里跪着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔」——膝盖一弯，人就矮了一截

root: 古英语动词 cneowlian / cneolian（跪下），与名词 cneo「膝」同源，共有一个后来不发音的 k；中古英语 knelen，过去式由 knelede 缩为 knelt，美式另作 kneeled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the physical act of going down on the knees, the same act as a sign of respect, and the prayer made in that posture.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：用膝着地的身体动作，同样动作所表示的敬意，以及在这个姿势里所做的祈祷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body lowering until its weight rests on the knees.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体下沉，直到重量落在双膝上。

branches.en: THE BODY: the plain movement from standing to resting on the knees.
branches.cn: 身体线：从站立到以膝支撑的直白动作。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: the low posture becomes a sign of honour or surrender.
branches.cn: 姿态线：低下的姿势成为致敬或臣服的标志。

branches.en: THE PRAYER: in many traditions prayer is made on the knees.
branches.cn: 祈祷线：许多传统中祈祷就是在膝上完成的。

branches.en: THE ROOT LINE: the verb and the noun knee share one Old English origin.
branches.cn: 词根线：这个动词与名词 knee 共有一个古英语来源。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: knelt and kneeled are both accepted past forms.
branches.cn: 形式线：knelt 与 kneeled 都是可接受的过去式。

intro.en: Kneel is a native verb whose family is small: inflection, a few suffixes, and the noun knee beside it.
intro.cn: kneel 是本土动词，词族很小：词形变化、几个后缀，以及一旁的同源名词 knee。

latinIntro.en: Kneel has no Latin ancestry; the Latin words below refer to the same posture only as comparisons.
latinIntro.cn: kneel 没有拉丁语血统，下面这些拉丁词只是同一姿势的对照。

items.meaning: to go down on the knees

items.example: The man kneeling is a guide.
items.exampleCN: 跪着的那个男人是向导。

items.meaning: one who, or a thing for
items.example: It forms kneeler, a kneeling cushion.
The knee rests on the cushion.

items.exampleCN: 它把 kneel 变成 kneels。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from genu and flectere

definition_en: a cutting instrument with a blade and usually a handle, or to injure someone with such a blade
core_image: 一片薄刃贴着砧板落下，把菜切成两半
scene: 灶前的灯下，菜板上堆着切好的葱段。She wiped the knife on a cloth and put it back in the wooden block.
sceneCN: 这里 knife 是「刀、菜刀」（第 1 个义项：带刃的切割工具），句意是她在布上擦了擦刀，把它放回木刀架。画面里有灶前的灯、菜板与切好的葱段。

pos.zh: 名词：刀；小刀；餐刀；刀片
动词：用刀刺伤；切割

derivatives.zh: knife 的不规则复数，义为「多把刀」
knife 与 edge 合成，义为「刀锋；十分危急的处境」
pen 与 knife 合成，义为「小折刀」
knife 与 man 合成，新闻用语指「持刀者」

senses.title: A cutting tool with a blade
senses.definition: a tool or weapon with a sharp blade fixed in a handle, used for cutting
senses.definitionCN: 刀片固定在柄上的切割工具或武器
senses.example: This knife is too blunt to cut tomatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀太钝，切不动西红柿。
senses.why: The core object is a blade with a grip, the simplest tool humanity has ever made.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是一片带握柄的刃，是人类造过的最简单的工具。

senses.title: A table knife for eating
senses.definition: a knife used at the table for cutting or spreading food, paired with a fork
senses.definitionCN: 餐桌上用来切或抹食物的刀，常与叉子配对
senses.example: Set a knife and fork beside each plate.
senses.exampleCN: 在每个盘子旁放一副刀叉。
senses.why: The tool entered the dining room and took on a fixed shape, with a rounded tip and a dull edge.
senses.whyCN: 这件工具走进餐厅并固定了形状：圆头、不锋利的刃。

senses.title: To stab with a knife
senses.definition: to wound or kill someone by pushing a knife into the body
senses.definitionCN: 用刀刺入人体使人受伤或死亡
senses.example: The attacker knifed him in the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 袭击者用刀刺了他的手臂。
senses.why: The tool name turned into a verb by naming the act of using it, a pattern English uses often.
senses.whyCN: 工具之名转为动词，用以命名使用它的动作，这是英语常见的模式。

senses.title: The blade in a machine
senses.definition: a cutting blade that forms part of a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 构成机器或工具一部分的切削刀片
senses.example: The knife on the cutter needs changing.
senses.exampleCN: 切割机上的刀片需要更换。
senses.why: Industrial parts keep the old name because their job is still to cut.
senses.whyCN: 工业零件沿用旧名，因为它们的仍是切割的活。

intro.en: Knife reached English from Old Norse, and its plural knives is one of the classic examples of English consonant change.
intro.cn: knife 由古北欧语进入英语，其复数 knives 是英语辅音变化的经典例子。

items.en: The Norse noun knífr named a short blade, and it came into English with the Norse settlers.
items.cn: 北欧语名词 knífr 指短刃，随北欧移民进入英语。

items.en: The native English word for a cutting blade was seax, which was gradually replaced by the Norse word.
items.cn: 英语本土表示刀刃的词是 seax，后来渐渐被北欧词取代。

items.en: The word appears as knif, and the k at the start had already stopped sounding.
items.cn: 这个词写作 knif，词首的 k 此时已不发音。

items.en: The plural knives shows the old rule that a voiceless f becomes v between vowels.
items.cn: 复数 knives 体现了旧规则：清音 f 在两元音之间变为 v。

items.en: The noun also became a verb, and today a person can be knifed in the street.
items.cn: 名词也转为动词，如今可以说有人在街头被刀刺伤。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words and forms of the same word; the near-meaning group gathers other cutting tools.
note.cn: 形近组收同样 k 不发音的词与本词的其他形式；近义组收其他切割工具。

entries.definition: The irregular plural, with f changed to v.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则复数，f 变为 v。

entries.definition: Another silent-k word, naming a mounted warrior.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 k 不发音的词，指骑士。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and means a rounded handle.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指圆形的把手。

entries.definition: The cutting part of a knife, or a whole cutting tool in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 刀的切割部分，正式用法中也指整件刀。

entries.definition: A long bladed weapon held with both hands, far larger than a knife.
entries.definitionCN: 以双手握持的长刃武器，比刀大得多。

entries.definition: A cutting tool with two blades that close on each other.
entries.definitionCN: 两片刃对合的切割工具，即剪刀。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Norse origin, the voiced plural, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用北欧来源、浊化的复数，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Norse knífr replaced the native seax, which survives in Saxon.
normal.cn: 北欧语 knífr 取代了本土的 seax，后者只留在 Saxon 一词里。

normal.en: Plural knives changes f to v, as in wife to wives.
normal.cn: 复数 knives 把 f 变成 v，如同 wife 变 wives。

normal.en: The k is silent, as in knee, knit and knock.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knit、knock 一样。

normal.en: A knife and fork is the fixed pairing on a Western table.
normal.cn: a knife and fork 是西餐桌上固定的搭配。

normal.en: Under the knife means having surgery, with the surgeon blade as the image.
normal.cn: under the knife 意为接受手术，用的是外科刀的意象。

abstract.en: A knife has two faces: one side feeds people, the other hurts them, and the same word covers both.
abstract.cn: 刀有两副面孔：一面养活人，一面伤害人，同一个词兼指两者。

abstract.en: Its usefulness lies in a single narrow line where all the force is gathered.
abstract.cn: 它的用处就集中在一条极窄的线上，所有力量都聚在那里。

abstract.en: Every cutting tool is a controlled accident: sharpness kept in a handle until it is needed.
abstract.cn: 每件切割工具都是受控的意外：锋利被收在柄里，直到需要时才放出。

examples.en: He cut the bread with a long knife.
examples.cn: 他用一把长刀切面包。

examples.en: The chef keeps her knives razor sharp.
examples.cn: 这位厨师的刀磨得极快。

examples.en: A young man was knifed near the station last night.
examples.cn: 昨晚一名年轻人在车站附近被人用刀刺伤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈夫」——一刀下去，菜就断成两截

root: 古北欧语 knífr（短刃），随北欧移民进入英语，取代了本土词 seax；中古英语 knif，词首 k 不发音；复数 knives 保留了 f 在两元音间浊化为 v 的旧规则；名词后转为动词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the cutting tool, the table version, the act of stabbing with it, and the blade inside a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：切割工具本身，餐桌上的那一把，用它刺人的动作，以及机器上的刀片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin sharp edge pressed along a board until the material parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道薄而锋利的边压着砧板，直到材料分开。

branches.en: THE TOOL: a blade in a handle, the oldest cutting instrument.
branches.cn: 工具线：柄上加刃，是最古老的切割器具。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the dining knife has a rounded tip and a dull edge.
branches.cn: 餐桌线：餐刀头圆刃钝。

branches.en: THE WEAPON: the same object turned against a body becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 武器线：同一物件转而针对身体，就成了动词。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: industry keeps the word for any cutting blade.
branches.cn: 机器线：工业界沿用它指任何切削刀片。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the plural knives shows f turning into v.
branches.cn: 形式线：复数 knives 显示 f 变 v。

intro.en: Knife is a Norse loan whose family grows by irregular plural, compounds, and a verb use.
intro.cn: knife 是北欧语借词，其词族靠不规则复数、合成与动词用法扩展。

latinIntro.en: Knife comes from Norse rather than Latin; the Latin cutting words below are contrasts, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: knife 来自北欧语而非拉丁语，下面这些拉丁语切割词是对照，不是祖先。

items.structure: knife with f changed to v
items.example: The knives are in the drawer.
He was knifed in the alley.
items.exampleCN: 他在小巷里被人用刀刺伤。
这起刀伤案震动了小镇。

items.example: He opened the letter with a penknife.

items.meaning: the sharp edge, or a critical state
items.example: The race is on a knife-edge.

items.exampleCN: 它把 knife 变成 knifes。

definition_zh: 编织；针织；使紧密结合；接骨愈合
definition_en: to make cloth or a garment by looping yarn with needles, or to join things closely, as a bone or a group may join
core_image: 两根针把一根线一针一针连成一片毛布
scene: 冬夜的沙发上，毛线球慢慢变小。She sat by the window and knit a scarf while the kettle began to hum.
sceneCN: 这里 knit 是「编织、针织」（第 1 个义项：用针把毛线连成织物），句意是她坐在窗边织围巾，水壶开始响起来。画面里有冬夜的沙发、毛线球与窗。

pos.zh: 动词：编织；针织；使结合；愈合
名词：针织衣物、编织样式

collocations.zh: 一针下、一针上（编织术语）

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「编织、编织物」
加 -er 构成，义为「编织者」
knit 与 wear 合成，义为「针织衣物」
合成形容词，义为「关系紧密的」

senses.title: To make cloth by looping yarn
senses.definition: to make a fabric or garment by interlocking loops of yarn on needles or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 用针或机器把毛线的线圈互相套住，织成织物或衣服
senses.example: Her grandmother knit him a thick woollen hat.
senses.exampleCN: 他奶奶给他织了一顶厚羊毛帽。
senses.why: The core act is joining loops, so that a long single thread becomes a surface.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是接合线圈，使一根长长的单线成为一片面。

senses.title: To join closely together
senses.definition: to unite people or things so closely that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把人或事物连得极紧，使其如同一体
senses.example: Shared hardship had knit the team together.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的艰难把队伍紧紧连在一起。
senses.why: Because knitting makes separate loops into one surface, the word easily describes people joined in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 因为编织把一个个分开的线圈连成一整片，这个词很自然地用来描述同样结合的人。

senses.title: To heal and join, of a bone
senses.definition: of a broken bone, to grow back together and become whole again
senses.definitionCN: 指断骨重新长合，恢复完整
senses.example: The broken rib will knit in about six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 断掉的肋骨大约六周就能长合。
senses.why: A healing bone closes the same way cloth does, thread by thread, so medicine borrowed the weaver word.
senses.whyCN: 愈合的骨头像布一样一针一针合拢，医学便借用了织工的词。

senses.title: To draw brows together
senses.definition: to draw the eyebrows closely together, usually in worry or thought
senses.definitionCN: 多因忧虑或思考把眉毛挤在一起
senses.example: He knit his brows at the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他读信时皱起了眉。
senses.why: Drawing brows together is the same gesture of closing a gap, so the weaving word serves for the face.
senses.whyCN: 把眉毛挤在一处正是在闭合缝隙，于是织工的词也用到了脸上。

intro.en: Knit comes from an Old English verb for tying a knot, and its meaning shifted from knotting to looping yarn.
intro.cn: knit 源自古英语表示「打结」的动词，词义由打结转为把毛线绕成线圈。

items.en: The verb cnyttan meant to tie or fasten with a knot, often used of nets and snares.
items.cn: 动词 cnyttan 意为打结、系扎，常用于网与陷阱。

items.en: The related German knoten and Dutch knopen keep the knot sense in the modern languages.
items.cn: 相关的德语 knoten 与荷兰语 knopen 在现代语言里仍保留打结义。

items.en: In Middle English the word could already mean both tying and forming loops of yarn.
items.cn: 到中古英语时，这个词已同时指打结与绕成线圈。

items.en: The looped-cloth sense wins, and the older knot sense survives in the related word knot.
items.cn: 绕线圈的布料义胜出，打结义则留在相关的 knot 一词里。

items.en: Metaphors spread: bones knit, teams knit, and people speak of a close-knit family.
items.cn: 比喻四处扩展：骨能长合，队伍能连紧，人们也说起 close-knit 的家庭。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words close to knit; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of making cloth or joining things.
note.cn: 形近组收与 knit 接近的 k 不发音词；近义组收其他织布或连接的方式。

entries.definition: The knot word from the same Old English root, now naming the tied loop.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古英语词根的「结」，如今指系出的绳结。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and names a mounted warrior.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指骑士。

entries.definition: Missing the k, and names the egg of a louse.
entries.definitionCN: 少了 k，指虱卵。

entries.definition: To cross threads lengthwise and widthwise on a loom, unlike the loops of knitting.
entries.definitionCN: 在织机上经纬交错，与针织的绕圈不同。

entries.definition: To make cloth with a single hooked needle.
entries.definitionCN: 用一支带钩的针做织品。

entries.definition: To join cloth with thread and a needle by stitching.
entries.definitionCN: 用针线缝合布料。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real knot origin, the two past forms, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的「打结」来源、两种过去式，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: The oldest sense is to tie a knot, which is why knot and knit are relatives.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是打结，所以 knot 与 knit 是亲属。

normal.en: British English prefers knitted; American English also uses knit as the past.
normal.cn: 英式英语偏好 knitted，美式英语也把 knit 用作过去式。

normal.en: Knit doubles the t before -ed and -ing: knitted, knitting.
normal.cn: knit 在加 -ed、-ing 前要双写 t：knitted、knitting。

normal.en: Knit together is the everyday metaphor for a united group.
normal.cn: knit together 是与团结相关的日常比喻。

normal.en: Close-knit describes a family or team that holds together tightly.
normal.cn: close-knit 描述紧密相依的家庭或团队。

abstract.en: One thread is weak; thousands of loops make a fabric that holds the body warm.
abstract.cn: 一根线脆弱，几千个线圈却能织成一面裹住身体的布。

abstract.en: Knitting is a slow addition: each loop shrinks the distance to a finished thing.
abstract.cn: 编织是缓慢的加法：每一个线圈都缩短了与成品的距离。

abstract.en: A bone joins and a friendship joins in the same verb, because both close a gap loop by loop.
abstract.cn: 骨头长合与友谊结合用同一个动词，因为二者都是一圈一圈地闭合缝隙。

examples.en: She knits while listening to the radio.
examples.cn: 她边听收音机边编织。

examples.en: The small village is a close-knit community.
examples.cn: 这个小村子是一个关系紧密的社区。

examples.en: The two bones knitted cleanly within two months.
examples.cn: 两块骨头在两个月内干净地长合了。

dict_mnemonic.text: knit 原是打结，一针一针打下去就成了织物

root: 古英语 cnyttan「打结、系扎」，与 knot 同源，同出于日耳曼语；中古英语兼指打结与绕线，现代英语以「针织」为主义，并引申出结合、愈合、皱眉等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: making cloth from loops, joining people closely, a bone healing together, and drawing the brows together.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：用线圈织成布，把人紧密连起，骨头长合，以及把眉毛挤在一起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two needles pulling one thread into a chain of loops that becomes cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根针把一根线拉成一串线圈，最终成为布。

branches.en: THE CLOTH LINE: interlocking loops turn one thread into a surface.
branches.cn: 布料线：互相套住的线圈把一根线变成一片面。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE LINE: close relations are described with the weaver word.
branches.cn: 人际线：紧密的关系用织工的词来描述。

branches.en: THE BONE LINE: medicine borrowed the verb for joining broken parts.
branches.cn: 骨线：医学借这个动词表示接合断处。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: brows drawn together repeat the closing of a gap.
branches.cn: 面部线：把眉毛挤在一起，重复了闭合缝隙的动作。

branches.en: THE KNOT LINE: the oldest sense survives in the related word knot.
branches.cn: 结线：最古老的意思留在相关的 knot 一词里。

intro.en: Knit is a native Germanic verb; English extends it with suffixes and compounds such as knitwear.
intro.cn: knit 是本族日耳曼动词，英语用后缀与 knitwear 一类合成来扩展它。

latinIntro.en: Knit has no Latin ancestor, so the Latin joining words here serve only as comparisons.
latinIntro.cn: knit 没有拉丁语祖先，这里的拉丁语连接词只作对照。

items.example: Her knitting is on the chair.

items.exampleCN: 这是一支紧密团结的队伍。
他们把俱乐部紧紧凝聚在一起。

definition_zh: 敲；敲门；碰撞；撞倒；敲门声
definition_en: to hit a door or surface with the hand or an object, often to be let in, or to strike something and make it fall or move
core_image: 指节落在木门上，发出短促的三下响声
scene: 旅馆的木门半旧，走廊里亮着一盏昏黄的灯。He knocked three times, then waited until a tired voice told him to come in.
sceneCN: 这里 knock 是「敲、敲门」（第 1 个义项：用手或物件敲打门面以示意），句意是他敲了三下，等人用疲倦的声音叫他进去。画面里有旅馆走廊、木门与昏黄的灯。

pos.zh: 动词：敲；敲门；碰撞；撞倒
名词：敲击；敲门声；挫折

derivatives.zh: 加 -er 构成，义为「门环、叩门者」
knock 与 out 合成，义为「击倒获胜；出众的人或物」
合成词，义为「可拆装的；压倒性的」
合成词，义为「闹剧式的、粗笨却结实的」

senses.title: To hit a door to be admitted
senses.definition: to strike a door with the hand so that people inside will open it
senses.definitionCN: 用手击门以让里面的人开门
senses.example: Someone knocked at the door just after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜刚过就有人敲门。
senses.why: The core act is a short strike on a hard surface, loud enough to be heard inside.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是在硬面上短促一击，声音刚好让屋内的人听见。

senses.title: To strike something and hit it
senses.definition: to strike a thing or a person, often by accident or with some force
senses.definitionCN: 撞上某物或某人，常属意外或带有力量
senses.example: The branch knocked against the window all night.
senses.exampleCN: 树枝整夜撞着窗户。
senses.why: From hitting on purpose the word widens to any collision, whether intended or not.
senses.whyCN: 从有意击打扩大为任何碰撞，不论是否有意。

senses.title: To make something fall
senses.definition: to cause something to fall or move by striking it
senses.definitionCN: 击打使某物倒下或移开
senses.example: He knocked the cup off the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他把杯子从桌上撞掉了。
senses.why: A blow that pushes an object off its place is the same action aimed at the thing rather than the door.
senses.whyCN: 把东西打离原位的这一击，用的是同一动作，只是目标换成了物件而非门。

senses.title: A blow or a setback
senses.definition: an act of striking, or a difficulty that sets a person back
senses.definitionCN: 击打的动作，或使人受挫的困难
senses.example: The team took a heavy knock when its captain left.
senses.exampleCN: 队长离开后球队受到沉重打击。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical blow and turns it into an image of bad luck.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了实实在在的一击，又把它转成厄运的比喻。

senses.title: The sound of knocking
senses.definition: the short sharp sound made by striking a door or a hard surface
senses.definitionCN: 敲击门或硬面所发出的短促响声
senses.example: A sharp knock came from the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机里传来一声尖锐的敲击声。
senses.why: The sound is the most detachable part of the blow, so the word names it on its own.
senses.whyCN: 声音是击打中最能单独剥离的部分，于是这个词也单独指这种声音。

intro.en: Knock first appears in English in the Middle Ages, probably from a Germanic root for striking, and its k has been silent for centuries.
intro.cn: knock 在中世纪才出现于英语，可能源自表示「击打」的日耳曼语词根，词首的 k 已静音数百年。

items.en: The verb is not recorded in Old English, though the related noun cnocc named a lump or knock.
items.cn: 古英语中未记录这个动词，但相关名词 cnocc 指肿块或一击。

items.en: Knock appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of striking hard.
items.cn: knock 于十四世纪出现，义为「重击」。

items.en: A relation with German knacken and Dutch knakken, both meaning to crack, is generally accepted.
items.cn: 普遍认为它与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken（意为「裂响」）有关。

items.en: The phrase knock at the door fixes the everyday sense of asking for admittance.
items.cn: knock at the door 这一说法固定了「示意求入」的日常义。

items.en: Particles multiply the senses: knock out, knock down, knock over, and knock off.
items.cn: 小品词使义项增多：knock out、knock down、knock over、knock off。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers silent-k words and relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of hitting.
note.cn: 形近组收 k 不发音的近形词与同族词；近义组收其他表示「击打」的动词。

entries.definition: Starts with the same silent k and names a tied loop of rope.
entries.definitionCN: 同样以不发音的 k 开头，指绳结。

entries.definition: One letter away, meaning a special skill.
entries.definitionCN: 只差一个字母，意为「窍门、技能」。

entries.definition: The word plus -er, naming a door ring or a person who knocks.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -er，指门环或叩门者。

entries.definition: To touch lightly and quickly, much softer than a knock.
entries.definitionCN: 轻而快地触及，比 knock 轻得多。

entries.definition: To hit noisily and heavily, with a louder result.
entries.definitionCN: 重而响地撞击，声音更大。

entries.definition: To hit something with a dull, accidental thud.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然撞上，声音沉闷。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real phrase family, the particle combinations, and the silent k that runs through the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的搭配家族、小品词组合，以及贯穿全词的不发音 k。

normal.en: The k stays silent, as in knee, knife and knot.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knife、knot 一样。

normal.en: Knock at the door is the phrase for asking to come in.
normal.cn: knock at the door 是请求进屋的说法。

normal.en: Particles change the result: out is a fight, down is a fall, over is a spill.
normal.cn: 小品词改变结果：out 是打斗，down 是倒下，over 是打翻。

normal.en: Two negatives make a compliment: she is a knock-out.
normal.cn: 两重否定反成赞语：她是惊艳众人的人。

normal.en: A knock on the engine is a warning sound, not a touch.
normal.cn: 发动机里的 knock 是警告声，不是触碰。

abstract.en: A knock is a question asked in sound, and the silence after it is the answer.
abstract.cn: 敲门是用声音提出的问题，之后的那片安静就是回答。

abstract.en: Any collision is a knock, because the same short shock passes through two objects.
abstract.cn: 任何碰撞都是一次 knock，因为同一股短促的冲击从两个物体之间传过。

abstract.en: From a fist on wood to a setback in life, the word keeps the image of something arriving suddenly.
abstract.cn: 从拳头落上木板到人生受挫，这个词始终保留着「突然到来」的意象。

examples.en: Please knock before you enter the office.
examples.cn: 进办公室之前请先敲门。

examples.en: The wind knocked the flowerpot off the sill.
examples.cn: 风把花盆从窗台上撞了下来。

examples.en: There was a loud knock at the back door.
examples.cn: 后门上响起一声很响的敲击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹克」——指节一闹，门就咚咚克响

root: 中古英语 knocken（始见于十四世纪，义为「重击」），可能源自日耳曼语中表示裂响的词根，与德语 knacken、荷兰语 knakken 相关；词首 k 不发音，后靠小品词扩展出 knock out、knock down 等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: knocking on a door, any striking collision, causing something to fall, a hit as a setback, and the sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：敲门，任何撞击，把东西撞倒，作为挫折的一击，以及那种敲击声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knuckles striking a wooden door, three short sounds in the quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：指节落在木门上，安静里响起三下短声。

branches.en: THE DOOR LINE: a knock is a request to be let in.
branches.cn: 门线：敲门是请求被放进来。

branches.en: THE IMPACT LINE: anything struck may move, fall or break.
branches.cn: 冲击线：被击中的东西会移动、倒下或破碎。

branches.en: THE FORTUNE LINE: a blow becomes a setback in life.
branches.cn: 命运线：一击变成人生里的挫折。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the noise of the blow can stand alone.
branches.cn: 声音线：击打的声音可以单独成义。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: the silent k ties it to knee and knot.
branches.cn: 形式线：不发音的 k 把它与 knee、knot 连在一起。

intro.en: Knock is a Germanic verb that English expands mainly through particles and compounds, not affixes.
intro.cn: knock 是日耳曼动词，英语主要通过小品词与合成来扩展它，而非词缀。

latinIntro.en: Knock has no Latin source; the Latin striking words below are contrasts.
latinIntro.cn: knock 没有拉丁语来源，下面这些拉丁语击打词只是对照。

items.example: He was knocked out in round two.
They knocked down the old wall.
The cat knocked over the vase.

items.meaning: one who or a thing that

definition_zh: 结；绳结；节（速度单位）；打结；（肌肉）紧绷
definition_en: a fastening made by tying a piece of rope or thread into itself, a unit of speed used at sea, or to tie something in this way
core_image: 一根绳在手里绕两圈，两端一抽，鼓出一个死结
scene: 码头的木桩上缠着好几道旧缆绳。The sailor pulled the wet rope tight and tied a firm knot around the post.
sceneCN: 这里 knot 是「结、绳结」（第 1 个义项：绳子自身系成的扣结），句意是水手把湿绳拉紧，在柱子上系了一个牢结。画面里有码头木桩与旧缆绳。

pos.zh: 名词：结；绳结；节（航速单位）；纠结
动词：打结；使紧绷；打结系住

derivatives.zh: 加 -y 构成，义为「多结的；棘手的」
knot 与 work 合成，义为「编织花饰」
slip 与 knot 合成，义为「活结」
加 -ed 构成，义为「打了结的；纠结的」

senses.title: A fastening tied in rope
senses.definition: a place where rope, string, or hair is tied and pressed together into a lump
senses.definitionCN: 绳、线或头发被系住并挤成一团的地方
senses.example: He made a loop and pulled a knot tight.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出一个环，把结拉紧。
senses.why: The core object is a fastening that holds by friction, made from the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心物件是靠摩擦自持的系扣，材料本身就是扣件。

senses.title: A unit of speed at sea
senses.definition: a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour
senses.definitionCN: 等于每小时一海里的速度单位
senses.example: The ferry was doing eighteen knots across the channel.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮以十八节的速度穿越海峡。
senses.why: Sailors measured speed with a knotted log line, and the number of knots counted became the name of the speed.
senses.whyCN: 水手靠打了结的测速绳测速，数到的结的数目就成了速度之名。

senses.title: To tie something in a knot
senses.definition: to tie or press something into a knot, or to fasten with knots
senses.definitionCN: 把东西系成结，或用结来固定
senses.example: She knotted the scarf around her neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把围巾在脖子上打了个结。
senses.why: The noun of a fastening turns into the act of making one, as with many object words.
senses.whyCN: 系扣之物转为制出系扣的动作，许多器物词都走这条路。

senses.title: A tight feeling or problem
senses.definition: a tight feeling in the chest or stomach, or a difficult complication in affairs
senses.definitionCN: 胸腹发紧的感觉，或事情纠缠难解的麻烦
senses.example: A knot of anxiety tightened in his stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 他胃里一阵焦虑紧缩。
senses.why: A knot holds fast and will not loosen, which is exactly how a worry or a difficulty feels.
senses.whyCN: 结扣得牢、不肯松开，忧虑与麻烦给人的感觉正是如此。

intro.en: Knot is an old Germanic word with a silent k, and the nautical use grew out of a knotted measuring line.
intro.cn: knot 是古老的日耳曼语词，词首的 k 不发音，航速义来自打了结的测速绳。

items.en: The noun cnotta meant a knot in rope or in hair, and the k was still pronounced.
items.cn: 名词 cnotta 指绳索或头发上的结，那时 k 还发音。

items.en: German Knoten and Dutch knot keep the same noun today, together with the related verb knoten.
items.cn: 德语 Knoten 与荷兰语 knot 至今保留同一名词，以及相关动词 knoten。

items.en: The k at the start stopped sounding, so knot became a homophone of not.
items.cn: 词首 k 不再发音，knot 与 not 成了同音词。

items.en: Sailors counted the knots on a trailing log line, and a speed of one knot meaning one nautical mile per hour grew from it.
items.cn: 水手数拖曳测速绳上的结，一 knot 表示每小时一英里海里的速度由此而来。

items.en: The verb and the figurative senses appear: hair, brows, muscles and worries all knot.
items.cn: 动词与比喻义随后出现：头发、眉毛、肌肉与忧虑都能打结。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers close spellings and relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other fastenings and tangles.
note.cn: 形近组收相近的拼写与同族词；近义组收其他系扣与缠结的说法。

entries.definition: The word plus -y, meaning full of knots or difficult.
entries.definitionCN: 本词加 -y，义为「多结的、棘手的」。

entries.definition: Sounds exactly the same, but it is the negative word.
entries.definitionCN: 读音完全相同，但是否定词。

entries.definition: The related verb from the same Old English tying root.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古英语系扎词根的相关动词。

entries.definition: A confused mass of thread or hair, without a deliberate fastening.
entries.definitionCN: 线与头发乱成一团，并非有意系成。

entries.definition: A knot tied with two loops for decoration or fastening.
entries.definitionCN: 用两个环系成的蝴蝶结。

entries.definition: A bend of rope that returns on itself, one half of a knot.
entries.definitionCN: 绳自身折回的环，常是结的一半。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the silent k, the nautical history of the speed sense, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用不发音的 k、航速义的海事来历，以及这个词常见的搭配。

normal.en: Knot sounds exactly like not, yet means the opposite of looseness.
normal.cn: knot 与 not 读音相同，意思却与「松」相反。

normal.en: Tie the knot is the everyday idiom for getting married.
normal.cn: tie the knot 是「结婚」的日常习语。

normal.en: At sea, one knot is one nautical mile per hour.
normal.cn: 在海上，一节等于每小时一海里。

normal.en: Knot doubles the t: knotted, knotting.
normal.cn: knot 要双写 t：knotted、knotting。

normal.en: A knotty problem is one full of knots that will not pull apart.
normal.cn: a knotty problem 就是满是解不开的结的难题。

abstract.en: A knot is made of the rope itself: the material holds, yet it is nothing but the material bent back on itself.
abstract.cn: 结由绳自身形成：材料在起作用，而它不过是材料折回自身。

abstract.en: Every knot is a decision that must be untied later, which is why difficulty and rope share a word.
abstract.cn: 每个结都是一项日后必须解开的决定，所以绳子与困难共用一个词。

abstract.en: The speed unit is a knot on a line thrown behind a ship, a number turned into motion.
abstract.cn: 航速单位源自抛在船后的测速绳上的一结，把数字变成了运动。

examples.en: The knot in the shoelace was too tight to pull open.
examples.cn: 鞋带上的结太紧，拉不开。

examples.en: The ship held a steady twelve knots all night.
examples.cn: 那艘船整夜保持十二节的稳定航速。

examples.en: Anxiety knotted his stomach before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前焦虑让他胃里发紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「脑特」——脑子特别绕，像绳子打了个死结

root: 古英语 cnotta「绳结、发结」，源自共同日耳曼语，同源于德语 Knoten、荷兰语 knot；中古英语词首 k 静音；航速「节」源自水手数测速绳上的结；后引申出打结、紧绷、棘手等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: a tied fastening, the nautical speed unit, the verb of tying, and the tight feeling or difficulty it resembles.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：系成的结，航速单位，打结的动作，以及结所比喻的紧绷感与难题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rope wound on itself and pulled into a hard lump that will not slip.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子绕回自身，一拉成硬块，不再滑动。

branches.en: THE ROPE LINE: the knot is a fastening made of the rope itself.
branches.cn: 绳索线：结是用绳本身做成的系扣。

branches.en: THE SEA LINE: counted knots on a log line became the unit of speed.
branches.cn: 海上线：测速绳上数出的结成了速度单位。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the object word becomes the verb of tying.
branches.cn: 动作线：器物词转为打结的动词。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: what holds fast without loosening becomes worry or trouble.
branches.cn: 感受线：牢住不放的东西成了忧虑或麻烦。

branches.en: THE SOUND LINE: the silent k makes it a twin of not.
branches.cn: 读音线：不发音的 k 让它与 not 成为双胞胎。

intro.en: Knot is a native Germanic word whose family is built by inflection, a few suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: knot 是本族日耳曼词，其词族由词形变化、少数后缀与合成构成。

latinIntro.en: Knot has no Latin source; the Latin words below are comparisons for the idea of binding.
latinIntro.cn: knot 没有拉丁语来源，下面的拉丁词只是「系缚」这一概念的对照。
